claims: Google has agreed to a $135 million class-action settlement regarding allegations that Android devices transmitted data to Google using cellular data without user permission.
U.S. residents who used an Android device on a cellular network since Nov. 12, 2017, may qualify for a payment.
U.S. residents who used an Android device with a cellular data plan to access the internet between Nov. 12, 2017, and the final approval date meet the eligibility criteria.
No claim form is required for automatic payment if you received a notice.
FederalCellularClassAction.com is the site to select a preferred payment method (PayPal, Zelle, etc.).
The final approval hearing is June 23, 2026.
The lawsuit is Taylor v. Google LLC.
Taylor v. Google LLC claimed that Android devices were programmed to transfer information to Google in the background even when not actively in use, consuming personal cellular data.
